requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

task.description: Run SECURITY-REVIEWER's gate against ELIXIR-DEV's initial implementation of the Letflow.Help context module (REQ-364), scoped against security-invariants.md's INV-1..INV-9, with particular weight on REQ-364's AC2 (a write attempting raw HTML/script content is rejected). Verify the write-path sanitizer's real behavior directly -- do not trust ELIXIR-DEV's own summary of what it blocks.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable invariant (INV-1..INV-9) is verdicted APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE, none silently skipped

The write-path markdown sanitizer is probed with at least one adversarial payload per plausible bypass class, reproduced directly against create_changeset/2, not assumed from the design or implementation summary
PASS only if no bypass survives reproduction; otherwise FAIL naming the exact bypass, the code path responsible, and the required fix

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- <path>`), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away.

BLOCKER: lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex's @markdown_link_pattern regex only matches CommonMark inline link/image syntax [text](url)/![alt](url). It does not match reference-style link/image definitions ([text][ref] ... [ref]: javascript:alert(1)), which any conformant downstream markdown renderer resolves into a real href/src. contains_unsafe_link_scheme?/1 returns false for such payloads (no [...](...) substring exists), so validate_no_unsafe_link_scheme/2 adds no error and the row is written with a javascript: payload live in body -- a complete bypass of REQ-364's own AC2 write-path sanitization requirement.

NON-BLOCKING FINDING: create_draft/2's `with` has an else clause mapping {:error, :invalid_schema_name} -> {:error, :invalid_prefix}, but update_draft/3, publish/2, reconfirm/2, withdraw/2 have no else clause, so an invalid prefix on those falls through as the raw {:error, :invalid_schema_name} instead of the documented {:error, :invalid_prefix} in their @specs. Not a crash, but a real spec/implementation inconsistency for REVIEWER.

SCOPE-CREEP FLAG RESOLVED: withdraw/2 (live->draft, added because design section 2's lifecycle diagram shows this transition though REQ-364's acceptance criteria don't name it separately) reviewed for independent security concern -- none found, follows the identical with-chain/prefix-scoping pattern as every other function. Scope-creep question itself deferred to REVIEWER, not a security finding.

result.next_action: Route back to ELIXIR-DEV for rework round 1 -- extend the URL-scheme scan to reference-style link-definition lines (e.g. ^\s*\[[^\]]+\]:\s*(\S+)), applied post-code-stripping the same way as the existing inline check, OR reconsider design section 5.3 option 2 (a real sanitizer/parser) given a regex denylist over markdown's full link-syntax surface has now demonstrated a concrete gap.
